name: Ribeye Steak Sandwich — with Caramelized Onions, Provolone and Horseradish Mayo
subtitle: with Caramelized Onions, Provolone and Horseradish Mayo
description: A dry-brined ribeye seared hard and sliced thin, piled on toasted ciabatta with jammy onions, melted provolone, peppery arugula and a sharp horseradish mayo. Serves 2.

ingredients.text: 450 g boneless ribeye steak, about 2.5 cm thick
ingredients.item: boneless ribeye steak, about 2.5 cm thick

steps.text: Season 450 g boneless ribeye steak, about 2.5 cm thick all over with 1 tsp kosher salt and refrigerate uncovered at least 45 minutes (or up to overnight).

Cook 1 large yellow onion, thinly sliced with 1 tbsp butter (for the onions) and 1/4 tsp salt (for the onions) in a skillet over medium-low for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until deep golden and jammy. Set aside.
Mix 3 tbsp mayonnaise, 1 tbsp prepared horseradish and 1 tsp Dijon mustard.

Pat the steak dry. Heat 1 tbsp neutral oil in a cast-iron pan over high until smoking. Sear the steak 4 minutes per side, flipping every 1 minute for an even crust, until 52°C inside for medium-rare. Add 1 tbsp butter for the last 1 minute and baste. Season with 1/2 tsp black pepper and rest 10 minutes.
Toast the cut sides of 2 ciabatta rolls, split in the steak pan for 1 minute, until golden.
Slice the steak thinly against the grain. Pile it on the bottom halves with the onions and 4 slices provolone, and broil 1 minute to melt the cheese.
Spread the tops with horseradish mayo, add 30 g arugula, close and cut in half.

notes: Slicing thin against the grain is what makes a steak sandwich bite cleanly instead of pulling out in one piece. Drizzle the resting juices over the meat before closing the sandwich.
